package_info.package_versions: 26 open-source NetBeans Java projects (various versions, not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The Octopus Scanner malware was injected into legitimate open-source NetBeans Java projects on GitHub, turning them into supply chain attack vectors. The malware infects developer environments, steals sensitive information, and propagates itself by further infecting built artifacts, enabling widespread compromise of developer systems and downstream users.

execution_context.file_location: build scripts (e.g., build.xml, project build files) within infected NetBeans projects

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At build-time, the code checks if it is running in a NetBeans environment, infects all projects in the workspace by modifying their build scripts, drops the malware payload, and exfiltrates sensitive data to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts should not self-replicate or modify other projects, nor should they exfiltrate data or drop additional payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build scripts automate compilation and packaging, not malware propagation or data theft.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build tools may update dependencies or perform code analysis, but not self-replication or exfiltration.

execution_context.file_location: malicious payload dropped into project output (e.g., JAR files)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects developer credentials and environment information, then sends this data to a command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Application code should not collect and exfiltrate developer credentials or environment variables.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate application code processes user data, not developer credentials or environment details.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Crash reporting tools may collect environment info, but with user consent and no credential theft.
key_indicators: Network communication to external C2 server

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into open-source NetBeans Java projects' build scripts on GitHub.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infection of developer environments during project build

attack_chain.action: When a developer builds the infected project, the build script infects all other projects in the workspace and drops the malware payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation of malware to additional projects and artifacts

attack_chain.action: The malicious payload is included in built artifacts (e.g., JAR files) and executed when these artifacts are run.
At runtime, the payload collects sensitive information (e.g., credentials, environment variables) and exfiltrates it to a remote command-and-control server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data and can further compromise affected systems

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts that modify other projects or replicate code
Unexpected network connections during build or runtime
Artifacts (JARs) containing code for credential harvesting or C2 communication
file_indicators: Modified build.xml or other build scripts with obfuscated or suspicious code
Unexpected files or payloads dropped in project directories
JAR files with embedded credential-stealing code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains or IPs during build or artifact execution
Unusual HTTP/S POST requests containing environment or credential data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build scripts in open-source projects for unauthorized modifications, especially code that replicates itself or drops additional payloads. Analyze built artifacts for embedded credential-stealing or network communication code. Monitor developer environments and build processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially during build or artifact execution. Use static and dynamic analysis to detect credential harvesting logic in Java code.
